reason: While the text references the Israelite people (הָעָם) as a collective group, they are depicted as passive recipients of divine commands and restrictions rather than as characters with agency. The people are instructed to sanctify themselves, wash their garments, remain prepared, avoid ascending the mountain, and refrain from approaching women—all directives they must follow. No individual people are named or portrayed with personal characteristics, decision-making autonomy, or independent action. All narrative authority and agency belongs to God (YHWH) and to Moses as His intermediary. The people are managed and constrained rather than portrayed as active agents shaping events.
